draft.title: A significant person in Christianity
card: A significant person is someone whose beliefs and actions changed how Christianity developed or how it is lived. Their influence reaches beyond their own time.
Paul of Tarsus

a first century follower of Jesus who travelled around the Mediterranean. He taught that Gentiles (non-Jews) could join the church without keeping all Jewish law, and his letters became part of the New Testament.
Martin Luther
a German monk who taught that people are saved by faith, not by good works or payment. His challenge to church practices in 1517 led to the Protestant Reformation and the Protestant churches.
Catherine McAuley
an Irish woman who founded the Sisters of Mercy in Dublin in 1831. The sisters put faith into action by caring for the poor, the sick and the uneducated, and the order spread to Australia.
draft.remember: A significant person is judged by the lasting effect of their beliefs and actions on Christianity.

a.q: Which description best shows why Martin Luther is a significant person in Christianity?
opts: His teaching on faith led to the Protestant Reformation
His letters to early churches became New Testament books
He founded a religious order to care for the poor in Dublin
He taught that Gentiles could join the church freely
a.why: Luther's teaching that people are saved by faith, and his challenge to church practices, led to the Reformation and new Protestant churches. The letters to early churches describe Paul, who is the most tempting wrong option because both men shaped Christian belief.
a.clue: Think of 1517 and the split in Western Christianity.

b.q: A school in Sydney run by the Sisters of Mercy teaches students to serve people in need. Which significant person's beliefs and actions does this most directly continue?
opts: Catherine McAuley, who served the poor and the sick
Paul of Tarsus, who taught that Gentiles could join
Martin Luther, who taught salvation by faith alone
Martin Luther, who founded the Sisters of Mercy
b.why: Catherine McAuley founded the Sisters of Mercy to care for the poor, the sick and the uneducated, and the order spread to Australia. Luther is the tempting wrong choice because he is well known, but he did not found the Sisters of Mercy.
b.clue: Which person founded the order named in the question?

a.best: His teaching on faith led to the Protestant Reformation

b.best: Catherine McAuley, who served the poor and the sick
